# Licensed speech specimens

These two short human-recorded greeting specimens are engineering inputs, not learner recordings or certified pronunciation teaching. Their exact source pages were inspected on 26 October 2026 through Firecrawl; original bytes were downloaded from the linked Wikimedia file URLs.

- `japanese-konnichiwa.wav`: こんにちは, by **Nesnad**; [original file and attribution](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Wikibooksqsjapanese1-snd005.ogg). The source's structured audio transcription identifies the greeting.
- `mandarin-nihao.wav`: 你好, by **Sjors Provoost**; [original file and attribution](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Zh_n%C7%90_h%C7%8Eo.ogg). The source identifies Mandarin pronunciation of 你好 / nǐ hǎo.

Both audio assets, including these converted versions, are distributed under **[Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)**. Changes: decoded from Ogg Vorbis and converted with FFmpeg to mono 16-bit PCM WAV, 16000 Hz; speech was not edited. No licensor endorsement is implied. This asset license does not change the surrounding original application code's license.

`manifest.json` pins each converted byte hash, duration and original attribution. The complete greeting occupies one segment spanning the full file; no phoneme/word alignment is fabricated. The files support meaningful short-phrase listening/dictation rather than only synthetic player tones. They do not qualify long-form listening, pronunciation scoring, actual learner microphone capture or native-speaker review.
